summary:
MYOSHIELD is an AI-powered orbital biotelemetry and crew health surveillance web platform built for deep-space missions. Powered by five live machine learning models trained on spaceflight physiological datasets, MYOSHIELD analyzes multi-domain crew telemetry across radiation exposure, musculoskeletal strength retention, and vestibular stability in real time—detecting both isolated anomalies and compounded, additive-synergistic health risks before clinical symptoms appear.

To bridge the gap between raw sensor data and immediate action in microgravity, MYOSHIELD pairs predictive diagnostics with an automated Audio-Assisted Crew Triage system that delivers looping auditory alarms and hands-free, step-by-step emergency instructions—such as limb immobilization and ARED load reduction—so astronauts can respond without looking at a screen. It also features Myo, an interactive astronaut companion synced to daily exercise countermeasures to keep crews engaged and mission-ready.

As human missions venture farther from Earth where communication delays make real-time ground support impossible, MYOSHIELD empowers crews with autonomous, life-saving medical decision support.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

MYOSHIELD is an autonomous, real-time crew health surveillance and countermeasure platform built for deep-space missions. When orbital biotelemetry (.csv) is uploaded, a FastAPI backend runs five machine learning models across Radiation, Musculoskeletal, and Vestibular health domains. Unlike traditional single-threshold monitors that evaluate vitals in isolation, MYOSHIELD detects compounded additive-synergistic physiological risks across domains before acute clinical symptoms emerge.

To translate predictions into immediate action in microgravity, MYOSHIELD features:

  • Audio-Assisted Crew Triage: When critical anomalies or synergistic risks occur, a looping Web Audio two-tone alarm and Web Speech synthesis protocol dynamically read out step-by-step emergency instructions (e.g., limb immobilization, ARED load reduction, distal pulse survey) so astronauts can respond hands-free without looking at a display.
  • Interactive Countermeasure Companion ("Myo"): An onboard Space Bear Astronaut companion—paired with an interactive first-time visitor tour—dynamically wakes up and energizes as crew members complete their daily exercise countermeasures, reinforcing preventative adherence.

Benefits & Intended Impact

On Lunar Gateway or Mars missions where communication delays of up to 20+ minutes each way prevent real-time Mission Control intervention, MYOSHIELD empowers crews with onboard medical decision support, lowers cognitive load during emergencies via hands-free voice triage, and helps prevent long-duration muscle atrophy and bone loss through engaging countermeasure tracking.

Data Sources & Google Colab ML Training Pipeline

We synthesized telemetry schemas, physiological thresholds, and validation suites (nominal, additive, and anomaly test scenarios) from seven peer-reviewed spaceflight and biomedical repositories:

  • Radiation Domain: NASA OSDR RadLab (visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/radlab) modeled spacecraft cabin dose rates (mSv/day), cumulative 7-day exposure (mSv), and South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) orbital spikes.
  • Musculoskeletal Domain: NASA OSDR Study OSD-684 (osdr.nasa.gov/bio/repo/data/studies/OSD-684, SpaceX CRS-21 skeletal muscle tissue chip) and Journal of Proteome Research (pubs.acs.org, Vol. 16/7, proteome-wide spaceflight muscle adaptations) parameterized microgravity fiber shifts, strength retention (%), and atrophy rates.
  • Vestibular Domain: NASA NTRS Citation 20260002549 (ntrs.nasa.gov, HRP CIPHER neuro-vestibular flight study), NASA NLSP Apollo Flight Crew Vestibular Assessments (nlsp.nasa.gov), and ICPSR Study 235362 (icpsr.umich.edu, aVOR eye movement and head kinematics) defined postural sway (cm), gaze stability (%), and motion sickness thresholds.
  • Systemic Biotelemetry: PhysioNet BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset (physionet.org/content/bidmc/1.0.0) provided continuous vital-sign time-series baselines (heart rate, respiration, and SpO2 variability) for systemic anomaly benchmarking.

Model Training Workflow: All preprocessing, feature engineering, cross-domain interaction modeling, and model evaluation were executed in Google Colab using Python, Pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn. We trained and validated five specialized classification and anomaly-detection pipelines, serialized them with joblib, and deployed them to our live FastAPI inference server for real-time CSV scoring.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • ML Training & Data Science: Google Colab, Python 3.11, scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, Joblib.
  • Backend: FastAPI, Uvicorn (deployed on Render).
  • Frontend: React / Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Web Audio API (AudioContext), Web Speech API (speechSynthesis) (deployed on Vercel).
  • AI Disclosure: Large Language Models (LLMs) were used during development to assist with code generation, UI refinement, and debugging.

Creativity & Human-Factors Considerations

Spaceflight stressors compound across physiological systems rather than acting alone; modeling additive-synergistic risk mirrors real aerospace medicine. We paired this predictive engine with microgravity-focused UX—combining a low-glare dark interface and hands-free voice triage with an emotionally engaging companion (Myo) to support both emergency safety and long-duration crew morale.
